items.title: The Week That Was, The Week Ahead: Macro and Markets, November 8
items.take: U.S. stocks ended a turbulent week in the red as the tech selloff, midterm results and AI-spending worries piled up. Friday's surprisingly strong 165,000-jobs print complicates the rate-cut story, which makes Tuesday's October CPI the week's centerpiece.

items.title: Wall Street Week Ahead
items.take: Inflation and AI are back in focus, with October consumer prices due Tuesday and consensus looking for headline inflation around 3.7%, airfare posting another notable increase. Post-election volatility still hangs over technology stocks.

items.title: The Week Ahead: CPI and Tech Earnings Test a Fragile Stock Market
items.take: Tuesday's CPI and Friday's PPI will shape whether the Fed raises at its December 8-9 meeting. The AI trade's second test comes from earnings at CoreWeave, Cisco and Applied Materials.

items.title: First Receivers · #1 · Sunday, November 8, 2026
items.take: Money did not leave the stock market last week, it left the most crowded names: the chips broke first and the flows rotated into companies making and powering physical things. The Dow's best day in 19 months Wednesday, then the AI trade broke.

items.title: Inflation and Earnings Test the AI Trade in the Week Ahead
items.take: Anthropic reportedly committed $3.4 billion for 1.7 gigawatts of gas-generator capacity for AI data centers, per an FT report relayed by Reuters. Reuters also cites LSEG data putting the odds of a December rate hike around 80% after the jobs beat.

items.source: Morgan Stanley Thoughts on the Market
items.title: Why the Bond Market Remains Calm After the Blue Wave
items.take: Friday's rotation pick: Morgan Stanley's Friday episode on why bond yields barely budged as the tech swoon deepened, and what that calm says about where the market thinks the risk sits.
